A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BLADE research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation benchmarks, inference timings, component ablations, human preferences, and qualitative comparisons on CogVideoX-5B and Wan2.1-1.3B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds two qualitative comparisons in its visual gallery.

M1.justification: ASA sampling, Gilbert rearrangement, threshold masking, global tokens, additive bias, and TDM objectives remain unchanged. ASA_GT becomes ASA_G, and the three algorithms are reordered and relocated without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the JourneyDB-derived training prompts, text-to-video task, two evaluated models, and benchmark coverage. The additional drone and Elsa gallery examples remain within the existing task and do not establish distinct evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding quantitative and human comparisons. RaA is newly discussed explicitly in Section 4.3, but it already appears alongside STA, SVG, and ASA in v1 Table 3.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated typical distillation budget from 250–500 to 100–200 iterations. The principal evaluation settings remain unchanged, including eight-step comparisons and the training-free procedure's first two dense-attention steps. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds qualitative baseline-versus-ASA_G comparisons for a drone and Princess Elsa in Figures 8 and 12. Existing rearrangement and global-token/additive-mask ablations, human evaluation, and attention-mask visualization are retained.

E5.justification: Removing v1 Appendix B also removes its sampled-maximum rank variance, standard deviation, and 68%, 95%, and 99% confidence calculations. This changes analytical uncertainty reporting, not experimental run counts. Table 7 retains seed 42, and neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for benchmark scores.

E6.justification: The numerical benchmark, timing, ablation, and human-preference results in Tables 1–6 are unchanged. v2 adds generated outputs for two gallery prompts while retaining the existing result images; these are additional qualitative results, not demonstrated numerical performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix B is removed entirely, including its formal setup, two assumptions, order-statistics analysis, Theorem 1, proportionality proof, and sparse-mask consistency argument. Section 3.3 also drops the associated theoretical-stability claim. v2 provides no replacement derivation.

C1.justification: The central data-free ASA/TDM contribution and headline efficiency-quality claims remain: 14.10× and 8.89× speedups and VBench-2.0 scores of 0.570 and 0.569. Superiority wording is trimmed from an introduction bullet but remains asserted in the method and comparison sections.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds a substantive rationale linking neighboring tokens' semantic similarity to shared masks and pooling. Section 4.3 explicitly interprets the retained RaA comparison, while Section 4.2 removes a broad generalization statement about model scales and video lengths. The main regularization explanation and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 7 removes the implementation class names WanTransformer3DModel and CogVideoXTransformer3DModel. The abstract replaces explicit public code-and-weights availability with a generic project-link statement at the same address; this does not establish actual resource withdrawal. Most implementation details and all pseudocode remain.

R1.justification: The O’Neill (2023) reference on order statistics is removed with the theoretical appendix. Positioning relative to TDM and existing sparse-attention methods otherwise remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title from Video-BLADE to BLADE, renames ASA_GT to ASA_G, adds Minqi Chen to the author list, and makes localized prose and cross-reference edits. Pseudocode and gallery organization change, but most narrative text and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised proportions and legend styling. Tables 2 and 3 become side-by-side displays, pseudocode is grouped in the appendix, and the gallery is reordered and expanded by two figures. Headers, citation colors, and Table 7 formatting also change without a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves table and pseudocode organization and adds two qualitative comparisons while preserving the quantitative evidence. It also withdraws v1 Appendix B's claim of identical masks, which its approximate proportionality argument did not establish. These are limited gains: no corrected theoretical guarantee replaces the removed analysis, some reproducibility detail is lost, and the shorter stated training budget is unexplained.
